items.title: City of Mississauga to implement hiring restrictions effective immediately
items.summary: One week into the term of Mississauga's new mayor and hiring restrictions are going into effect at the city. It comes after staff were directed by Mayor Alvin Tedjo to freeze property taxes for the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

items.title: Police did not plan to arrest Francique night of fatal Mississauga shooting, inquest hears
items.summary: A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Black man who was shot by police is hearing that officers did not plan to arrest the man the night of the fatal incident. Det. Mani Sharifi said police did not plan to arrest Jamal Francique in 2020 but did so when they observed him breaching his bail conditions by leaving his home. Sharifi says the plan was for police to continue surveillance on Francique, which they had been doing for roughly three or four days, when the opportunity for an arrest came up. Asked by a juror why Francique was not arrested earlier in the week when police first observed him breaching his bail, Sharifi said his unit was focused on investigating if the man possessed a firearm or was involved in any drug activity. , townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020. items.title: Bothersome beavers focus of upcoming town hall in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials will meet with residents in January to discuss ongoing efforts to stop beavers from disrupting water flow in the city’s northwest end. Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden said the city will host a virtual town hall on Jan. 13 to explain its beaver management strategy. Officials will outline how they plan to keep the critters from causing more problems in the Lisgar community, near the Milton border. Last fall and winter, the City of Mississauga removed several beaver dams and beavers from in and around Sixteen Mile Creek and Osprey Marsh in the heart of Lisgar. The animals, which were safely relocated, had built dams that caused drainage issues near the creek and marsh, disrupting local water flow, the city said. Despite the city’s removal efforts, residents reported spotting beavers back in the area this past spring. The sightings prompted McFadden to say she and City of Mississauga staff would keep an even closer eye on the situation as they search for a long-term solution. Fast-forward to earlier this month when McFadden told residents in her latest update that beavers, among the largest living rodents in the world, “continue to reside along the Sixteen Mile Creek running through Lisgar. “Despite previous efforts last winter to remove several beavers, another lodge and series of dams have been spotted further north within the tributary,” McFadden continued.

items.title: ‘This isn’t Vice City’: Driver caught at 200 km/h on GTA streets, police say
items.summary: Police are reminding residents to leave dangerous behaviour in the digital GTA after a driver was clocked going more than 200 km/h on Mississauga and Brampton streets. Grand Theft Auto IV released last week, letting gamers “live out fast cars, high speed chases and questionable life decisions,” Peel regional Police say. But police urged gamers not to take antics from Grand Theft Auto into the Greater Toronto Area on Monday, and used a high-speed traffic stop as a cheeky example of what not to do on the roads. A video released by police shows a vehicle speeding on roads in Mississauga and Brampton, and on the highway, reaching speeds of over 200 km/h. Police follow the driver in a helicopter, eventually tracking the vehicle to a residence. In real life, there are no respawns, no reset button, and very real repercussions. GTA 6 is finally here, but this driver may have spent a WAY too much time in Leonida as he was going over 200 km on our roads. Unfortunately for them, this isn’t a video game. With the help of Air3, officers safely tracked the vehicle from above and made an arrest. This is a reminder to keep the speeding, stunts, and getaway drives where they belong: in Vice City.

items.title: More health inspectors needed in Mississauga and Brampton to meet Ontario guidelines: report
items.summary: Peel Region needs to hire more public health inspectors in the coming year to meet Ontario guidelines, keep up with complaints and meet service requests, according to a review. Food safety complaints and service requests increased by 23 per cent from 2024 to 2025 in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, according to last year’s Peel Public Health review. Special events also spiked by 22 per cent during the same time period, putting additional pressure on the region’s inspectors. ” There were at least 43 Peel Public Health inspectors in 2025 with a median salary of $103,376, according to the Ontario Sunshine List. Ontario Public Health Standards doesn’t set a fixed inspector-to-population staffing ratio, but requires that local public health boards ensure they have qualified personnel to deliver mandatory inspection and enforcement programs under provincial legislation. Peel Public Health inspects retail food establishments, personal service settings, licensed child care centres, recreational water and tanning facilities, and tobacco and vaping retailers across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. Inspections use a three-colour sign system—Green (Pass), Yellow (Conditional Pass), and Red (Closed)—to rate facilities. The staffing shortage means inspections “are increasingly prioritized, delayed, or missed,” leading to an increased risk “of foodborne illness, unsafe environments, and preventable public health incidents,” the report reads.

items.title: Men charged after armed robberies at employment agencies in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Two men from Brampton have been charged following a string of armed robberies at employment agencies, police say. The gunpoint robberies all happened between April and August at employment businesses across Mississauga and Brampton, Peel Regional Police say. Investigators say masked suspects entered the businesses and confronted employees while armed with firearms. Police say knives were also used in some incidents, and that suspects stole cash, gift cards, electronic devices and other property in the hold-ups. The robberies resulted in losses exceeding $53,000, police say. Officers identified a pair of suspects through an investigation dubbed Project: Sega, and seized a stolen vehicle worth approximately $30,000 and two replica firearms. “Everyone deserves to go to work without fear of threats or violence,” Peel Regional Police Dep. Chief Nick Milinovich said in a statement. ” Peel police say Satnam Dhillon, 31, and Rajdeep Singh, 21, both of Brampton, have been arrested and charged with multiple counts of robbery and disguise with intent. Dhillon has also been charged with two counts of fail to comply with release order, possession of property obtained by crime and fail to comply with undertaking. Anyone with information about this incident can contact Peel Regional Police by calling 905-453-3311.

items.title: Shuttle Buses Fill In at Pearson Airport as Maintenance Cuts Automated Train Service to One Line
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Toronto Pearson Airport's Terminal Link train is running on a single track this week while crews carry out routine maintenance work. Airport officials say only one of the two fully automated, driverless trains is operating, with the reduced service taking effect early this week and continuing into next week. Shuttle buses are filling in between Terminal 1, Terminal 3 and Viscount Station while the second train is down, the airport says. The free trains normally link travellers to the Sheraton Gateway Hotel, the ALT Hotel and the Value Park garage and lot, officials note. When running at full capacity, the Terminal Link operates around the clock, with trips between stations typically taking two to eight minutes, according to the airport. Officials describe the temporary reduction as part of planned work meant to keep the line operating safely and reliably.

items.title: Arrest Made in Fatal Toronto Shooting of Mississauga Man, Second Suspect Still Wanted
items.summary: According to insauga.com, police have arrested one of two suspects wanted in the fatal shooting of a Mississauga man in Toronto. Officers found the victim with gunshot wounds on Saturday, Nov. 7 and performed life-saving measures before paramedics took him to hospital, where he died, making him Toronto's 33rd homicide victim of 2026. Police identified two suspects on Nov. 14 and issued Canada-wide warrants for Armani Callender, 19, and Cameron Marlor, 17, both of Toronto. On Sunday, Nov. 22, Toronto police announced they had arrested and charged Callender. He faces charges of second-degree murder, attempted murder, possession of a firearm while not holding a licence, and possession of a loaded regulated firearm. Marlor, the second suspect, remains outstanding, police say.
